name: The John H. Kinzie household
head: kinzie_john_h

arrival.note: A RETURN RATHER THAN AN ARRIVAL, AND THAT IS THE COMPLICATION. Kinzie was a child of the old Kinzie house on the north bank, went to Fort Winnebago as sub-agent, and is back at Chicago in business by 1834 when his advertisement runs and he is elected trustee. Nothing reached dates the return. 1834 is the earliest year the evidence forces. THE SETTLERS TABLE DATES A DIFFERENT EVENT AND THE VALUE THEREFORE DOES NOT MOVE. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830 (data/research/books/records/moses_kirkland_v1_actual_settlers_pre_1830.json). It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. Row bk_mose1_as_017 reads 'Kinzie, John H', nativity Canada, YEAR 1804, remarks 'Born July 7, 1803, died Jan. 21, 1865' — so the table's own remarks cell makes its year cell an arrival IN ARMS at ten months old, with his father's household. That is his first coming to the settlement and it is not the return this field records; the card says in terms that it is 'A RETURN RATHER THAN AN ARRIVAL'. A run reading 1804 into this field would be flattening two events fifty years of history apart into one number. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's own preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and its remarks are civic acts of 1825-1830. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here. A DATED PRESENCE IN THE TOWN, AND NOT AN ARRIVAL. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois, vol. 2 (1895), printed page 348 (claim bk_mose2_018; data/research/books/claims/moses_kirkland_history_of_chicago_v2.json) names the eleven gentlemen who organised the first Episcopal congregation in the city in 1834, eight of them its vestry. This man is among them, so he was at Chicago in 1834. THE YEAR IS LATER THAN THIS FIELD AND THEREFORE BOUNDS NOTHING: it corroborates a man already here and is recorded for that. THE GRADE CEILING IS THE SOURCE'S AND NOT THIS FIELD'S. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago, Illinois (1895) is a compiler sixty years after the fact; every claim taken off it is transcription_mediated and none is scan_verified, so nothing drawn from it is graded above `inferred` (the rule T-1322 set for the settlers table, kept here). AND IT CORROBORATES THE RETURN YEAR THIS FIELD ALREADY CARRIES. This card's 1834 is `inferred` and its note says "Nothing reached dates the return. 1834 is the earliest year the evidence forces" — the advertisement and the trusteeship. A second, independent 1834 sighting of John H. Kinzie in the town, organising a congregation and sitting on its vestry, is exactly the corroboration that note was waiting on. It does not date the return either, so the value and the grade are unchanged. THIS PROJECT HOLDS THREE KINZIES — John Harris, James and Robert Allen — and the compiler's "John H. Kinzie" reaches one of them; a bare `Kinzie` would have been refused, as T-0575 refused "the Kinzies".

party_size_on_arrival.note: Two named adults. Whether children were in the household in July 1835 is not established here; the Kinzie family's genealogy is in Andreas but was not worked for this parcel.

origin.value: Chicago, by way of Fort Winnebago
origin.note: He was born into the Chicago settlement; his wife came from Connecticut by way of Fort Winnebago, which is where Wau-Bun begins. The compound origin is this record's summary. A CONTRADICTION IS RECORDED HERE AND IS NOT RESOLVED. Row bk_mose1_as_017 of the settlers table prints his NATIVITY as CANADA, with 'Born July 7, 1803' in the same row's remarks — against this field's reading that he was born into the Chicago settlement. Both are retrospective secondary works and neither outranks the other on this project's ladder, so THIS RECORD PICKS NEITHER: the value stands as the reading that earned it and the table's disagreement is written beside it, where the next run with a primary record can settle it. Upgrading or overwriting on a tier-3 compilation would be manufacturing the certainty the sources have not got.

reason_for_coming.value: Family property and the forwarding trade
reason_for_coming.note: The Kinzie heirs owned a quarter interest in the north fractional half of Section 10, on which Kinzie's Addition was laid out - the land Charles Butler and Arthur Bronson came west to buy in 1833. The motive is the obvious reading of a family returning to its own land in a boom.

lives_at.note: NOT ATTESTED, AND ONE CANDIDATE IS EXPLICITLY RULED OUT. Charles Butler in 1833 recollected that the old Kinzie house on the north side 'had been previously destroyed by fire'; an 1830s list Andreas prints says it 'was then unoccupied and in a dilapidated state'. Either way it is not a residence for this household and this dataset does not model it.

works_at.note: The building record is graded inferred for a name reason this household inherits: Andreas's list says 'Jim Kinzie's store' and the 1834 advertisement says J. H. Kinzie, and those are two different men of the same family. The record follows the advertisement. This dataset also holds kinzie_hunter_warehouse under 'John H. Kinzie and Lieut. David Hunter', which is a second premises and is not linked here.

present_on_scene_date.note: Trustee and president through the 1834-35 municipal year and a delegate for District No. 3 in the city-charter conference of November 1836.

kin.note: JOHN HARRIS KINZIE IS THE HALF BROTHER OF JAMES KINZIE, IN THE FORM THE SOURCE GIVES IT. The mirror of the row on hh_kinzie_james, and written here because a kinship on one record only leaves this one still saying the two men were unrelated. Hurlbut's bracketed note under an American Fur Company outfit entry of 1821 reads '[The late James Kinzie, formerly of Chicago, and half brother of the late John H. Kinzie.]', filed as bk_afc_015 in data/research/books/claims/american_fur_company_hurlbut.json. HALF IS THE WHOLE POINT: the same father and different mothers, and it is the first thing a summary flattens. INFERRED RATHER THAN ATTESTED, AND THE GRADE IS WHAT AN 1881 EDITORIAL NOTE IS WORTH. This is not the town's contemporary paper but Hurlbut's own identification, printed sixty years after the consignment it annotates and after both men were dead, and this project reads it through Genealogy Trails' transcription rather than the original volume. It is a good source for the fact and it is still a recollection, so the relationship is reasoned from it rather than read off a record. A KINSHIP IS NOT A PLACEMENT. Nothing about either household's position, arrival, trade or membership rests on this row, and Hurlbut writing in 1881 about 1821 does not touch the scene date. What it does defend is the thing a shared surname keeps endangering: four household cards in this dataset are Kinzies — six until T-0839 folded two duplicate initials cards into their named men on 2026-09-05, which is the prior question T-0732 had to settle before it could rule on this family at all — data/research/books/crosswalk.json already has to refuse 'Mr. John Kinzie' the elder silversmith against John Harris Kinzie his son, and two men recorded as HALF brothers are two men, explicitly.

persons.note: PRESIDENT OF THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES FOR THE YEAR BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. He was elected a trustee at the second town election of 11 August 1834 and chosen president, and the 1834 roster is: 'J. H. Kinzie, President; Isaac Harmon, Clerk and Collector; J. S. C. Hogan, Treasurer.' Whether he was still president on 1 July 1835 depends on the date of the third election, which Andreas places only 'in July, 1835' - see the research note. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Kinzie, John” (tax_1833_062, line 114); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Kinzie, John H.” (poll_1834_067, line 236). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Kinzie' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). HALF BROTHER, NOT BROTHER, AND THE SOURCE IS AN EDITOR'S NOTE OF 1881. Hurlbut's bracketed note under the American Fur Company's 1821 consignment entry reads “[The late James Kinzie, formerly of Chicago, and half brother of the late John H. Kinzie.]” — the same father and different mothers, which is the form this dataset keeps, because flattening it to ‘brother’ is the move that lets the three Chicago Kinzies collapse into one another. The two men are kinzie_john_h in hh_kinzie_john_h and kinzie_james in hh_kinzie_james, and this project models them as separate households. Read as bk_afc_015 and cited to chicago_antiquities_american_fur_co. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it is an 1881 recollection about 1821, the ladder abstains on it (rung G5), and it moves no grade, no arrival, no placement and no household membership — both men are attested here on other evidence and stay so. THE LINK ITSELF IS THIS RECORD'S `kin` ROW, NOT THIS PROSE. T-0597 found that the residents schema had no field for a kinship BETWEEN two households; T-0704 then gave the layer one while this reading was in flight, and both records now carry the reciprocal half_brother row, graded inferred against this same source. What stands here is the READING that row rests on — the note as printed, the page it stands on and what an 1881 editorial note is worth — so the card cites its own evidence rather than asserting a link with nothing beside it. THE 1840 FEDERAL CENSUS — A HEAD FIVE YEARS AFTER THE SCENE, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1840 federal census of Chicago, read line by line off the left sheets in this repository, carries 1 head of this name — “John H. Kinzie” (33S7-9YYJ-W6, printed page 232, line 25). This project has ruled the head a MATCH for this person: the full name agrees, it is unique on both sides, and a discriminator independent of the name — directory persistence — separately places the same person in Chicago after the 1840 book was taken. Under the rule that decided it (L6 matched), by the crosswalk's own ladder (data/research/census_1840/resident_crosswalk.json). LATER EVIDENCE ONLY. The ratified grading ladder binds: an 1839 or 1840 appearance alone is never an 1835 resident, and 1840 household composition is never back-projected to the 1835-07-01 scene. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and an 1840 head is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'John S. Kinzie', printed once by the Democrat on 10 December 1833, is the forename of the documented John Harris Kinzie and the town holds no other John Kinzie in 1835.
merge_ruling.against_merge: The middle initial S contradicts H, and the Kinzie surname is precisely the one T-0839 warns about: four Kinzie men stand on the town's cards and this project has already mis-folded a Kinzie once (T-0732). C4 would fire here on a surname with one documented bearer of the forename; it is withheld because the owner named this family as the trap. His call.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('kinzie_john_h:age_bands_1840'). research_note: THE HOUSEHOLD THAT EXPOSES A DATE THE WHOLE OFFICER LAYER TURNS ON. Andreas says only that 'the third election was held in July, 1835' and then lists the officers it produced - H. Hugunin president, with W. Kimball, B. King, S. Jackson, E. B. Williams, F. C. Sherman, A. Loyd and George W. Dole as trustees. THIS PROJECT CANNOT SAY WHETHER THAT ELECTION HAD HAPPENED BY 1 JULY 1835. If it had not, the town's president on the scene date is John H. Kinzie and the 1834 board is in office; if it had, it is Hiram Hugunin. The town elections of 1833 and 1834 were both held on the tenth or eleventh of August, which is an argument that the 1835 one fell late in the month rather than at its start, but Andreas's own text says July. NO OFFICE-HOLDING CLAIM IN THIS PARCEL RESTS ON THE ANSWER, and the seven trustees of the 1835 board are deliberately not written as households on the strength of an election this project cannot date.
